about: Visible-grain targets: the spread of L* (CIELAB lightness, 0-100), a perceptual scale, so the same number looks about the same on any colour. grain.js solves the blend and opacity that hit them. Below ~0.45 grain is invisible.

confirmed.note: A production site's dark radial gradient fading in over off-white: 0.14 / 0.27 / 0.44 showed no visible difference, even Strong. At 0.5 / 0.8 / 1.4 the site owner picked Even (soft-light, 0.81 L*). Mid and light use the same targets because L* is perceptual; not yet confirmed by eye.

screens.about: Websites can't tell OLED from LCD; they can tell HDR screens (most OLED phones, XDR laptops) and the high-contrast setting. Targets above are for the reference screen the picks were made on. HDR screens show deep darks harder, so dark backgrounds get a little less grain there. High contrast gets less grain everywhere. Factors are a first guess, not confirmed by eye.
screens.referenceNote: Owner's picks were made on a standard-range P3 display (dynamic-range: high false), 2026-11-09.
